memory: In a study of 452 patients, 26.3% had P. vivax parasitaemia during follow-up. memory: In patients requiring casting, video-assisted remote consultations (RMC) resulted in longer mean consultation durations (29.0 min) compared to standard consultations (UNN, 22.6 min, p = 0.0063). No significant differences were observed in operated or discharged patients. Other studies showed no significant differences in force compensation or appetite response. Adverse events were more common with higher doses of gepotidacin but were mild. Smoking impacted immune cell counts, while vitamin E had limited effect. These findings suggest RMC may increase consultation time for casting subgroups, with no significant differences in other outcomes.

memory: The Sonas programme demonstrated significant improvements in MMSE scores compared to the reading group at T0 (p=0.011) and T1 (p=0.044), and to the control group at baseline (p=0.026). Differences in change over time were observed between Sonas and both the reading (p=0.019) and control groups (p=0.001). Data were collected at T0, T1, and T2. No overall significant effect on communication ability was found. Other studies indicated no significant differences in outcomes between home-based and centre-based training, or between alcohol and mechanical methods in refractive surgery.
text: The Sonas programme significantly improved MMSE scores compared to the control group at baseline (p=0.026) and showed greater change over time (p=0.001). These findings suggest a positive effect of the Sonas programme on cognitive function as measured by MMSE.

memory: The Sonas programme showed significant differences in MMSE scores compared to the reading group at baseline (p=0.026) and over time (p=0.011, p=0.044) for those with MMSE scores of 0–10. Other studies showed no significant differences in peakVO2, physical fitness, or refractive error between groups. No significant differences in coagulation parameters or satisfaction levels were found between home-based and centre-based training. memory: No significant difference in overall QoL between immediate and delayed treatment groups at baseline or follow-up (PMC2361520). Median survival was 13.0 vs. 11.0 months, with no significant difference in progression-free survival (PMC2361520). Other studies also found no significant QoL differences related to treatment timing. Cinaciguat reduced nitro-oxidative stress in DM patients (PMC4628236). Home telemonitoring did not improve emergency visits but increased costs (PMC3657667). Linagliptin improved HbA1c and reduced albuminuria compared to placebo (PMC3816860). No significant differences in recovery time or respiratory issues between Alfentanil and Remifentanil, though nausea/vomiting was higher with Remifentanil (PMC3591547).

DM60 showed better treatment retention and lower morphine levels compared to placebo.
